entry.summary: Lemma 1: The quantum token schemes IQT1 and IQT2 are eps_unf-unforgeable with eps_unf = (1/2 + 1/(2 sqrt 2))^N.

fields.label: Statement verbatim
fields.text: Lemma 1: The quantum token schemes IQT1 and IQT2 are eps_unf-unforgeable with eps_unf = (1/2 + 1/(2 sqrt 2))^N.

fields.label: Variables
fields.text: N: number of BB84 qubits Bob sends Alice (no losses in the ideal scheme)

fields.label: Definitions
fields.text:
eps_unf: 'eps_unf-unforgeable: probability that Bob accepts Alice''s tokens as valid at any two or more
  different presentation points is <= eps_unf, if Bob follows the scheme honestly (main text p.3).'

fields.label: Game definition
fields.text: Ideal two-presentation-point scheme (M=1). IQT1 (Table 1): B sends N BB84 states |phi_{t_k u_k}>. A measures each in random basis y_k, keeps outcomes x, sends d = y (z=0) or the bitwise complement of y (z=1) to B. In stage II, A chooses b, sends c = b xor z. B_i computes d~_i, and B_b validates x if x_b = t_b on Delta_b = {k : d~_{b,k} = u_k}. IQT2: A measures all qubits in one basis z. Dishonest Alice wins if she gets valid tokens at BOTH Q0 and Q1 (SI p.5: a_0 = t_0 and b_1 = t_1). Proof: Lemma 6 with gamma_err=0, beta_PB=0, theta=0 (O = 1/sqrt2), so lambda = 1/2 - 1/(2 sqrt2) and max ||D_{a,b}|| <= (1-lambda)^N.

fields.label: Assumptions
items: no losses, no errors, exact BB84 states, uniform bases/states (beta_PB = beta_PS = 0)
secure and authenticated classical channels among agents of the same party; secure labs
Bob honest (unforgeability is against dishonest Alice)

fields.label: Quantifier over adversaries
fields.text: general cheating strategy: joint projective measurement on the N qubits plus an arbitrary finite-dimensional ancilla (SI p.5)

fields.label: Tightness
fields.text: upper bound (no tightness claim found in the main text)

fields.label: Not valid for
items: W1 / W1_CV Wiesner games (different game; MVW W1_CV base is 3/4+sqrt2/8 = 0.9268, not 0.8536)
the realistic schemes QT1/QT2 with loss/noise/bias (use T-KLPR22-THM1)
2^M presentation points without the Theorem 2 pair-count factor
